back_translation: “As for you, take up a lament for the princes of Israel,
and say: ‘What was your mother? She was like a lioness among the lions; she lay down among the young lions and reared her cubs.
She raised one of her cubs until it became a young lion; it learned to tear prey, and it devoured men.
The nations heard of him, and he was caught in their pit; with hooks they led him away to the land of Egypt.
When she saw that she had waited in vain and her hope was lost, she took another of her cubs and made him a young lion.
He prowled among the lions and became a young lion; he learned to tear prey, and he devoured men.
He destroyed their strongholds and laid waste their cities; the land and all that filled it were terrified at the sound of his roaring.
Then the nations from the provinces all around set out against him; they spread their net over him, and he was caught in their pit.
With hooks they put him in a cage and brought him to the king of Babylon; they put him in custody, so that his roar would no longer be heard on the mountains of Israel.
Your mother was like a vine in your vineyard, planted by the water; it was fruitful and full of branches because of the abundant water.
It had strong branches fit for a ruler's scepter; it towered high above the thick branches, conspicuous for its height and its dense foliage.
But it was uprooted in fury and cast down to the ground; the east wind dried up its fruit; its strong branches were broken off and withered, and the fire consumed it.
Now it is transplanted into the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty land.
Fire has gone out from its main branch and consumed its fruit, so that no strong branch remains on it fit for a ruler's scepter. This is a lament, and it shall be used as a lament.’”
